content:
morgan: quick RFC follow-up — propose extracting KV cache ownership out of the runtime into a small Cache Control service to centralize eviction, prefix reservations, and tenant-level quotas. sketch + migration plan below.

jia: curious — won't an extra network hop add latency on hot paths?

morgan: good call. design intent: runtime keeps hot-prefix local cache for reads, control plane only handles lease/evict decisions and durable metadata. path for generation stays local for most ops; only misses/coordination touch cache-control.

alex: ok can you paste the minimal API you imagine?

morgan: here — rough gRPC idea:
```
service CacheControl {
  rpc ReservePrefix(ReserveRequest) returns (ReserveResponse);
  rpc EvictPrefix(EvictRequest) returns (EvictResponse);
  rpc QueryOwnership(QueryRequest) returns (QueryResponse);
}
```
fields are small: prefix, tenant_id, lease_ttl, reason.

jia: eviction decisions: centralized ML policy or simple heuristics?

morgan: start simple: LRU-ish by tenant + prefix score, then add async policy tickets for more advanced eviction. want separation so experiments don't touch runtime logic.

sasha: concerned about blast radius — this control service becomes critical path for leases. what's fallback if it flaps?

morgan: planned fallbacks: 1) runtime has fail-open mode that honors last-known leases for N seconds, 2) local soft-eviction that keeps serving until control-service confirms, 3) circuit-breaker + read-only degraded mode. will document SLOs and runbooks.

liam: metrics / observability? need per-tenant lease latency, evictions/sec, mistaken-evictions (regressions), and a roll-forward tracer to link prompts to evictions.

morgan: agreed. will add per-route tags, request ids, and rollouts gated on metrics. also will emit a small metric that counts cross-node lease lookups to track added hop.

alex: migration plan?

morgan: phased approach:
- phase 0: feature-flagged control-service in same cluster; runtime calls it but still authoritative locally (no enforced evictions).
- phase 1: control-service starts issuing advisory evictions; runtime can opt-in per-route.
- phase 2: control-service owns leases; runtime enforces evictions; fallback circuits enabled.
- phase 3: split infra to dedicated fleet and enable multi-region replicas.

jia: timeline? who owns it?

morgan: 6-week spike (me + jia) to validate perf; 8-week engineering sprint for phase 0/1 (eng-runtime + eng-platform); sasha for runbooks and oncall prep; liam for dashboards.

sasha: also add tenant ACL checks and make KMS keys available for eviction audit logs — compliance want that.

morgan: noted. will include KMS integration and audit-tag in proto.

cache-bot: deploy check: bucket size under limits, no conflicts. (automated note) :white_check_mark:

liam: one last thought — prefer we keep the API intentionally tiny. more state in runtime avoids network cost, but centralizing policy buys faster iteration and less tech debt. we should measure decision velocity vs p95 add.

morgan: yep — goal is to reduce ongoing ad-hoc eviction code in runtime (we have 7 different heuristics currently). central service = one place to evolve. we'll keep tight perf budgets, measurable gates, and an escape hatch to roll back to purely-local mode.

alex: sounds reasonable. put the mini-RFC into the rfc/ folder and ping infra for a capacity estimate.

morgan: will do. posting short doc now, thanks all. :pray:
